finding: Two of the four clubs playing Week 10 with no injury rows do read "No Injuries Reported" on the official hub (LAC, BAL). The other two do not: SEA and CIN now publish full blocks, and their rows were never ingested here. Treating an empty block as "healthy" would corrupt every availability model, and so would treating a missing block as an empty one. Corrected in this session — the original wording named SEA, CIN, LAC and BAL, which the live page contradicts (see FL-22).
evidence: Re-fetched 2026-11-12 22:40Z. The Monday block reads "Chargers / No Injuries Reported / Ravens / No Injuries Reported". The Seahawks block lists 14 players (AJ Barner, Anthony Bradford, Charles Cross, Sam Darnold, Derick Hall, Drew Lock, Quenton Nelson, Uchenna Nwosu, Patrick O'Connell, Connor O'Toole, Brandon Pili, Jarran Reed, Rashid Shaheed, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Leonard Williams). The Bengals block lists 4 (Jonathan Allen, Kyle Dugger, Dylan Fairchild, DJ Turner II).
decision_impact: Blocking: availability features must distinguish three states — reported, declared none, and absent from the file. The third state is a collection gap, not a fact about the club.

finding: At fetch time the official hub published game-status designations for only 6 of 254 Week 10 players (2 Commanders OUT, 1 Giant QUESTIONABLE, 3 Patriots OUT). Sunday and Monday designations were not yet in the file, so the who-is-out input is missing for 12 of 14 games.
evidence: 254-row ingest; 6 non-empty status cells and 6 non-empty injury cells, measured from the file
decision_impact: Blocking for Week 10 pricing: Q-20 open; re-pull required before kickoff

finding: The 2026 rosters contain cross-team movement that a naive pipeline would read as an error (Myles Garrett listed on LAR, Micah Parsons on GB, Mike Evans on SF, Deshaun Watson on CLE, Budda Baker and Josh Sweat on AZ, Za'Darius Smith on ATL, Quenton Nelson on SEA, A.J. Brown on NE, Kirk Cousins on MIN, Lucas Patrick and Chig Okonkwo on WAS). Nothing was corrected during transcription - rows are stored exactly as published. Four of these are independently confirmed on the same official page (Cousins trade, Watson start, Beck start, Lock start).
evidence: Injury hub rows cross-checked against the official Wednesday roundup
decision_impact: Blocking for joins: the 32-team roster sweep (S-15, Q-23) must run before any team-level model consumes these rows

finding: Official headline says Rams WR Puka Nacua is likely to be placed on IR with turf toe and sprained MCL/PCL; the official Wednesday roundup says per the head coach he will not be placed on IR, on roster-mechanics grounds, while still missing significant time. Both pages are NFL.com.
evidence: Two same-domain statements
decision_impact: Material: not-on-IR and out-for-significant-time imply different return windows, so IR status alone cannot be the availability key

finding: Roster-list mechanics the brief depends on (IR minimum games missed, count of return designations, the 21-day practice window, PUP/NFI treatment) were only locatable on third-party sites. The official operations site was checked and does not expose a fetchable rule page at the paths tried.
evidence: Negative result: the operations landing page links to game operations and programs pages, not to a roster-manual rule page
decision_impact: Blocking for gate wording: rule text must be obtained officially (S-14) before SIG-06 gets numbers

finding: There is no official public depth chart. The expected path returns an error page, so the requirement to know when second, third or fourth-string backups replace starters cannot be met by reading a depth chart at all; it must be reconstructed from roster status, practice participation, designations and actual playing time.
evidence: https://www.nfl.com/teams/new-england-patriots/depth-chart/ renders a 404 page titled "404 - Flag on the Play."
decision_impact: Blocking for R-20 and R-21: the Depth and Deficiencies page publishes the evidence and leaves depth-rank and effect columns blank

finding: The official standings table renders 16 value columns but the fetched markup exposes no header row; only W, L, T, PCT, PF, PA, net points and the streak string are unambiguous from format and arithmetic. The remaining split-record columns are omitted rather than guessed.
evidence: Division view and league view render the same unlabelled columns; the legend lists field names but not their order
decision_impact: Contained: seven of sixteen columns ingested. Later need for division or conference splits requires the underlying field names

finding: In the hub practice tables the Injury column is populated for only 6 of 254 rows; the rest are blank even where the same club's injuries are described in prose on the same site. Blanks are stored as published and are not backfilled from prose, because that would be an inference about which row matches which sentence.
evidence: Row-level comparison of the hub table against the Wednesday roundup
decision_impact: Material: body-part features cannot come from the hub table; they must come from the prose feed with an explicit join

finding: The hub presents one participation value per player per week as fetched; the Wednesday, Thursday and Friday progression that the practice-transition signal needs was not available as three stored filings. Trend signals cannot be built from a single snapshot.
evidence: The fetch captured one state of a page that changes three times a week
decision_impact: Blocking for SIG-01 and SIG-02: needs a snapshot scheduled per filing day, with the filing date stored

finding: No price data of any kind exists in this repo: no open or closing spread, total, moneyline or prop price, therefore no vig, no no-vig fair value, no CLV and no realised edge. Every quantitative claim about line origination is consequently blank on the site.
evidence: Repository inventory at session start: one file, README.md Update after the fourth session merged: a third-party historical price file did arrive (pipeline/data/raw/closing_lines.csv, 2006-2018 only) and a sparse 2026 moneyline field (163 of 272 games), neither of which changes this flag - see FL-21 and S-29.
decision_impact: Blocking for the entire origination objective (R-08). See Q-01

finding: The sandbox blocks outbound network access outside a package and repository allowlist, so unattended ingest from this environment is impossible today. All data here was obtained through the agent fetch tooling rather than by code that can re-run on its own.
evidence: Direct test: an HTTPS request to the league site from the shell failed at TLS connect while the fetch tool returned the same page
decision_impact: Determines architecture: snapshots plus staleness labels (S-01) now; a real ingest worker needs a runner with egress

finding: The repo contained no specification, no requirements file and no code before this session - one 6-byte README and one commit. The 40-row requirement register was reconstructed from the project brief in the conversation, which is not a durable addressable source of truth.
evidence: git log at session start: single commit 01f2271 with one tracked file
decision_impact: The register is the only written scope of the project; it needs owner sign-off to become authoritative

finding: Three rows in the depth log rest on article headlines only (Jets WR Garrett Wilson ruled out for the Madrid game, Falcons RB Brian Robinson out for the Madrid game, Ravens QB Tyler Huntley out for the season), because those roundup bodies were not fetched. They are marked headline-only in the source registry.
evidence: Rows tagged headline-only in data/sources.csv
decision_impact: Low impact: context rows, not inputs to any gate or number

finding: The roster status-code vocabulary was validated on one club and one partial page read (New England). Status showed ACT on every row in that chunk, so the IR, PUP and NFI code spellings are not yet confirmed from a fetched page.
evidence: Only the first of three chunks of one team roster page was read
decision_impact: Material to the availability graph: enumerate the status vocabulary from a full 32-team pull before hard-coding it

finding: Player URLs use disambiguated slugs with opaque suffixes for name collisions (josh-jacobs-x3315, noah-fant-x4946, david-edwards-x1290, tytus-howard-x1979, zachary-carter-x9168) and some slugs disagree with the displayed name (Chig Okonkwo is chigoziem-okonkwo, Jacob Hummel is jake-hummel, Kam Curl is kamren-curl, Chris Brooks is christopher-brooks, Gervon Dexter Sr. is gervon-dexter). Name-based joins will silently miss.
evidence: Slug list taken directly from the published hrefs
decision_impact: Sets the primary-key decision in Q-22: display names are not keys

finding: GitHub Pages for this repository is configured as a legacy build from the main branch root. The site must therefore live at the repository root; moving it into docs/ or a gh-pages branch changes the published layout.
evidence: Pages configuration read from the GitHub API at session start
decision_impact: Non-blocking, but any restructuring must update the Pages source in the same change

finding: The league does not use one stable code for the Los Angeles Rams: the standings table renders them LAR while the schedule and game pages render them LA. Any join between a standings-style table and a schedule-style table silently drops one club unless an alias is applied.
evidence: Both codes appear in official pages fetched 2026-11-12: nfl.com/standings shows LAR, the week-1 game page for SF at the Rams shows LA. The import normalises LA to LAR and the auditor reports 32 of 32 clubs reconciling only after that normalisation.
decision_impact: Material. Every future join to a fixture, injury or price table needs a canonical club key; without one, a nine-game record disappears without an error being raised. See S-28.

finding: The imported dataset contradicts itself: its meta block declares 122 games while the array it describes holds 136 rows. The published count is the array's, because that is the one that reconciles with the standings table; the metadata field is left as the owning session wrote it rather than corrected here.
evidence: data/games_2026.json meta.games = 122 vs len(games) = 136, printed by tools/import_parallel.py on every run.
decision_impact: Low for the site, which reads the array. A real trap for any other tool that trusts the summary field. Reported to the owning session rather than patched silently.

finding: The repository publishes four HTML trees and two tool suites at once: this audited dashboard at the root (legacy Pages build from main /), session arena-01b698ef's register dashboard under review/, and two builds of session arena-009ec582's site under archive/session-009ec582/ and docs/. Two CI workflows publish independently: .github/workflows/validate.yml audits the root build, verify.yml audits review/. tools/build_site.py and tools/verify.py were claimed by both sessions at merge time, so the review suite now runs as tools/review_build_site.py and tools/review_verify.py with their logic unchanged.
evidence: Pages configuration read from the GitHub API (build_type legacy, source main /), plus .github/workflows/pages.yml, .github/workflows/verify.yml and the merged tree itself.
decision_impact: This is why a root *.html file must never be hand-edited - it is generated, and the CI drift check fails the commit. It also means a reader cannot tell from the live URL which register is authoritative, and a new session can edit the wrong tree: see S-27.

finding: The imported game log covers weeks 1-9 only and stops the day before the week-10 slate this site is built around, so there is no continuous nine-week-plus-current-week series: any trend feature must be computed across a boundary where the two halves come from different fetches.
evidence: data/games_2026_wk1_9.csv max week = 9 against data/schedule_2026_wk10.csv week 10 fixtures; both fetched 2026-11-12 but the results file was assembled from week-by-week pages while the slate came from the injury-report page.
decision_impact: Blocks nothing, but it is the reason no form, rest-day or trend number is published on this site yet: closing week 10 into the log is a prerequisite for any of them. See S-26.

finding: The repository now contains market price files, and they are not usable as price evidence for the season this site analyses. pipeline/data/raw/closing_lines.csv holds 20,490 rows spanning 2006 to 2018 and zero rows for 2026; the only 2026 prices are a moneyline field inside pipeline/data/raw/games.csv, populated for 163 of 272 rows with no capture timestamp, no book identity and no revision history.
evidence: Counted in the merged tree from the two CSVs themselves (season min/max, per-season row counts, non-empty moneyline cells), not from that session's documentation.
decision_impact: FL-10 therefore stands: no vig, closing-line value or edge figure can be published from these files, and adopting them would replace a documented absence with an undocumented number. The decision is S-29.

finding: The landing page incorrectly attributed the complete multi-session site to "this session, in one branch." The statement has been corrected; the site history spans multiple documented sessions and merged PRs.
evidence: Previous sentence in content/index.md contradicted the repository coordination log and PR history; corrected in the current content source.
decision_impact: Resolved in prose; retain this review flag so readers can inspect the provenance correction.

finding: GitHub Pages API reports legacy publication from main at /, while .github/workflows/pages.yml also deploys an Actions artifact built from docs/. Both the root and /docs/ pages currently serve, but the intended source of truth and interaction between these deployment modes require owner review.
evidence: Observed API response: build_type legacy, source branch main, path /; repository workflow uploads docs/ and calls deploy-pages. Post-merge deployment checks succeeded, but this does not resolve which tree should be canonical.
decision_impact: Review and document one canonical deployment mode/path; do not change Pages configuration without verifying the intended published tree.

finding: The published Week 10 snapshot claims 28 clubs and omits three clubs that the official hub does populate. Of the 28 clubs playing Week 10, data/injuries_2026_wk10.csv holds 24. SEA (15 players) and CIN (4 players) are absent although the league publishes both in full, and IND carries 11 of the 13 rows published (CJ Allen, full participation, and Grover Stewart, did not participate, are missing). A hand-written empty-club list in tools/build_site.py — SEA, CIN, LAC, BAL — had been treated as the set of empty blocks and was stale in both directions.
evidence: Row-by-row comparison of every club block on the live hub against data/injuries_2026_wk10.csv: 25 of the 28 clubs matched exactly on name, position, practice status and game status; only SEA, CIN and IND differed. The four genuine "No Injuries Reported" states are LAC and BAL (published as such) plus the two that are simply absent (SEA, CIN).
decision_impact: Material: 15 SEA rows include the confirmed starting-quarterback change (Sam Darnold did not practice, Drew Lock limited), which is exactly the depth-chain evidence R-19 to R-21 depend on. The builder now derives the expected club set from the fixture list, and count claims are metrics rather than prose.

finding: data/depth_charts.json leaves the Kansas City left-tackle starter unasserted (a name collision was refused rather than guessed), so the first name in that group is the 2nd-string Diego Pounds. Any consumer that assumes "names[0] is the starter" will read Pounds as the KC LT starter. The same file omits two transcribed-nowhere third-string entries (Josh Downs WR, Marcus Harris DT) that the club does publish.
evidence: Re-fetched chiefs.com/team/depth-chart this session and compared all 22 groups: 19 exact. The LT group renders Kahlil Benson then Diego Pounds; the dataset holds only Pounds, and its own chart_corrections note records why. No published cascade is affected because Pounds is not on the Week 10 practice report.
decision_impact: Latent rather than active: nothing on the site is wrong today, but the next model that reads a depth chart needs an explicit "starter asserted?" flag per group instead of positional indexing. Fix belongs with the 32-club transcription (S-33).
